label: Episode 01
title: How graph databases work: Neo4j and Kùzu
subtitle: Before we build one in C++, why graphs, where the series is heading, and how Neo4j and Kùzu store a graph and run a query.
more: We start a series that builds smollerGraph, a small graph database, from scratch in C++, heading towards a knowledge graph that mvGPT can ask for facts. Before writing any code, we look at the property graph model, why following relationships beats joining tables for queries that walk many hops, and Cypher, on a small graph about animals. Then we run a food chain query on Neo4j and Kùzu, compare how each of them keeps its graph, and write a first graph in C++, kept in memory, with a walk down the food chain and GoogleTest tests. · Graph databases · Intro · Why graphs · Towards a knowledge graph · What a graph database is · Cypher · Neo4j · Kùzu · Side by side · Where to go deeper · What smollerGraph could be · The plan · A throwaway graph in C++ · Nodes and relationships · Facts from a file · Walking the graph · Tests · Wrap-up · graph database · knowledge graph · neo4j · kuzu · kùzu · cypher · gql · property graph · database internals · index-free adjacency · csr · embedded database · bloodhound · cybersecurity · ldbc · c++ · from scratch · smollergraph · mvgpt

label: Episode 02
title: Graph database in C++: pages on disk
subtitle: The graph moves from memory into files of 4 KiB pages, with fixed-size records for nodes and relationships, so it outlives the program.
more: We move smollerGraph's graph out of memory and onto disk, in pages of 4 KiB that a pager reads and writes, the way SQLite's file format does. Nodes and relationships become 32-byte records in those pages, with each node at the head of a chain of its relationships, as in Neo4j's record format, and the tests from episode one pass without a change. Along the way the code gets a Docker build and GitHub Actions, and sg load and sg walk keep the graph in a folder between runs. · Storage and indexes · Intro · Last time · Today · Docker and CI · Pages · Records in pages · The graph on disk · Two runs, one folder · What's slow, for now · Wrap-up · graph database · c++ · storage engine · pages · fixed-size records · record store · index-free adjacency · pread · pwrite · docker · github actions · googletest · database internals · from scratch · smollergraph

label: Episode 03
title: Graph database benchmark: Neo4j vs Kùzu
subtitle: A first benchmark on a million relationships, with the same two-hop question asked of smollerGraph, Neo4j and Kùzu.
more: We measure smollerGraph against Neo4j and Kùzu on a made-up social graph of a hundred thousand people and a million relationships, generated with a fixed seed so each machine gets an identical one. sg load reports how long loading takes, a new sg bench command times a two-hop walk from a thousand people, and a Python script loads the graph into Kùzu and Neo4j, in Docker, to ask them for those people too. label: Episode 04
title: Graph visualization in the browser with D3.js
subtitle: cpplint, clang-tidy and Abseil's Status for smollerGraph, then a UI, with sg serve answering HTTP and a page that draws the graph with D3, walks it a hop at a time, and shows each node's record on disk.

label: Episode 05
title: Database buffer pool in C++: keeping pages in memory
subtitle: A buffer pool for smollerGraph, with frames, a page table, pins, dirty pages and the clock, and what it does to a million relationships.
more: We give smollerGraph a buffer pool, the part of a database that keeps pages in memory, after counting the pages it reads and writes. Loading a million relationships read and wrote over six million of them, a system call each. The pool has frames, a page table, pins and dirty pages, and a clock that picks the page to evict. A latch keeps sg serve's threads out of each other's way, and we measure it all again against Neo4j and Kùzu, and look at why databases keep a pool of their own instead of using mmap. · Storage and indexes · Performance · Intro · Last time · Today · Counting pages · A buffer pool · Records through the pool · A latch for threads · The numbers again · What it costs · Wrap-up · buffer pool · database internals · page cache · clock algorithm · cache eviction · c++ · graph database · mmap · storage engine · neo4j · kuzu · database performance · smollergraph

label: Episode 06
title: B+ tree index in C++: finding a node by name
subtitle: An index on names for smollerGraph, a B+ tree in pages through the buffer pool, so opening a graph no longer reads each node.
more: We give smollerGraph an index on names, a B+ tree in a file of its own, read through the buffer pool, so opening a graph no longer reads each node to build a map of names in memory. Its leaves hold the names in order, the pages above them say which page holds which names, and splits grow it a level at a time. label: Episode 07
title: Writing a Cypher query parser and planner in C++
subtitle: A subset of Cypher for smollerGraph, from tokens to a parser, a plan and its rows, in sg query and in the UI.
more: We teach smollerGraph a subset of Cypher, the query language Neo4j and Kùzu speak, starting from a lexer and a recursive descent parser for MATCH patterns and what they RETURN. A planner turns a pattern into steps named after Neo4j's operators, a NodeIndexSeek through our B+ tree when the start has a name, an AllNodesScan when it doesn't, and an Expand for each hop, and EXPLAIN shows them. An executor runs the plan, sg query prints the answers, and the UI gets a query box for the questions we asked Neo4j in episode one. · Cypher · Intro · Last time · Today · Our subset · Tokens · A parser · A plan · Rows · Cypher in the UI · What's missing · Wrap-up · cypher · query parser · query planner · recursive descent parser · lexer · query execution · graph database · c++ · neo4j · kuzu · explain plan · database internals · smollergraph

title: Deploying a graph database to a VPS with Docker
subtitle: smollerGraph on a VPS, sent over SSH and run with Docker Compose, with Caddy serving the page in front of the database.
more: We put smollerGraph on a VPS with a small script, deploy.sh, which sends the committed code over SSH, and Docker Compose builds it there and runs it in two containers. Caddy serves the page and passes the API's requests on to sg serve, which nothing outside can reach. label: Episode 09
title: Property graph storage and WHERE in C++
subtitle: Properties for smollerGraph's nodes and relationships, in a chain of records on disk, loaded from facts, asked about with WHERE, and shown in the inspector.
more: We give smollerGraph's nodes and relationships properties, kept as in Neo4j's record format: a third file of 32-byte records, each with a key, a value and the next property's id, so a node's properties form a chain, like its relationships. The facts we load get properties in braces, read by our Cypher parser, and Cypher gets WHERE, with each filter planned as early as it can run, and RETURN of any property. label: Episode 10
title: Canvas vs SVG: drawing a Wikidata graph
subtitle: Mammals and birds from Wikidata in smollerGraph, with room in its records for real names and a label, and a page that draws what a query returns on a canvas, measured against SVG.
more: We load a real graph into smollerGraph: the mammals and birds on Wikidata, 21,834 species, genera, families, orders and classes. Their names don't fit, so nodes and properties get records of 64 bytes, and nodes get a label, which our facts and our Cypher learn to read. The page we built would draw every node with SVG, so we redo it: it draws what a query returns on a canvas, with a table, a plan, a history, a search and an inspector, and the server says what each query cost.
